- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) periods, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust future forecasts downward by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a price spike, model often fails to correct; apply lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast 2–3 days after sentiment dip.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted offset.
